body: Did you miss Platform & DevOps Engineering last week? The group took over Commence in Virginia Beach on Wednesday night for three talks that ran the whole range, with The AI Collective – Hampton Roads co-sponsoring. Mark Bennett opened with Letting Claude Take the Wheel and then proved the point live — a working PLaDO-inspired ecommerce site with a mock Stripe plugin, built from a single prompt and deployed while the room watched.

Tiffany Richardson-Harrell followed with How a Non-Technical Builder Uses Vibe Coding to Create Custom Apps, the view from someone shipping real tools without a traditional dev background. Yuriy Shyyan closed at the far end of the spectrum, demoing ClusterAPI standing up a production-grade Kubernetes cluster on the latest release — his verdict on doing that live: “when it comes to k8s demos, kubectl apply -f for the win.”
Thanks to Chandler Pitcher and Commence for hosting, and to Ted Patterson and The AI Collective – Hampton Roads for sponsoring the food and backing the AICHR + PLaDO collaboration.

quote.text: I was able to build this with one prompt in about 6 minutes and deploy it in about 4 minutes — all accessible over something OTHER than localhost. … Some parts of our jobs in the Platform space becomes making things with less friction, enjoyable, safe and secure, and fast.
